subject.title: Fix subagent announce restart recovery cascade

question: Should OpenClaw treat subagent completion announce handoffs as delivery-only turns that run without tools and reconcile to non-running after restart instead of human restart recovery?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent, but the permanent boundary between human turns, delivery turns, session recovery, and Codex native tools is a maintainer-owned security and session-state decision.

options.title: Merge bounded delivery-turn fix
options.body: Accept the PR's invariant that announce completion handoffs are delivery-only, tool-free turns and that interrupted announce runs should be marked non-running rather than recovered as human work.

options.title: Request broader recovery design
options.body: Ask the author to fold this into a wider restart-recovery model if maintainers want all non-human lifecycle turns classified through one explicit run kind before merge.

options.title: Pause for active-wake provenance work
options.body: Defer this PR only if maintainers want the adjacent active-wake provenance work to define the canonical announce handoff contract first.

recommendation.title: Merge bounded delivery-turn fix
recommendation.body: Accept the PR's invariant that announce completion handoffs are delivery-only, tool-free turns and that interrupted announce runs should be marked non-running rather than recovered as human work.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the densest recent history around subagent announce delivery helper ownership and related runtime seams.
